billing_account.description: The billing account to which the logging exclusion applies.
billing_account.rationale: Billing account selection ensures the exclusion is applied to the correct organizational scope and impacts cost management and access controls.
billing_account.compliant: Proper billing account ID with appropriate access controls

name.description: The name of the logging exclusion. Must be unique within the billing account.
name.rationale: Exclusion names should clearly indicate purpose and scope to ensure proper management and auditability of log filtering rules.
name.compliant: Descriptive names following organizational naming conventions (e.g., exclude-health-checks, filter-debug-logs)
name.non-compliant: Generic or unclear names that don't indicate exclusion purpose

description.description: A description of the exclusion's purpose and what log entries it filters out.
description.rationale: Clear descriptions help ensure proper understanding of what log data is being excluded and why, maintaining auditability and compliance.
description.compliant: Detailed description of exclusion criteria and business justification
description.non-compliant: Missing or vague descriptions that obscure exclusion purposes

disabled.description: Whether the exclusion is disabled. Defaults to false.
disabled.rationale: Exclusion status should be carefully managed to ensure only approved exclusions are active, preventing unintended loss of security-relevant log data.
disabled.compliant: false (for properly justified and approved exclusions)
disabled.non-compliant: true (for exclusions that should be active per policy) or improperly enabled exclusions

filter.description: The filter that determines which log entries to exclude. See [Advanced Log Filters](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/view/advanced-filters) for information on how to write a filter.
filter.rationale: Filter criteria must be carefully constructed to avoid excluding security-relevant logs while properly filtering noise and non-essential data.
filter.compliant: Well-defined filters that exclude only non-security-relevant noise (e.g., health checks, debug info)
filter.non-compliant: Overly broad filters that exclude security-critical logs or filters that could mask malicious activity
